The base hyperbola has parametric equations $x=7\sec t,\quad y=7\tan t$ on the given interval.

$$
f(t,z)=⟨7\sec  t,\,\text{_____},\,z⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,z)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${x}^{2}-{y}^{2}=49$ for $x\ge 7.$ What is the second component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the hyperbola ${x}^{2}-{y}^{2}=49$ for $x\ge 7$ in $xy$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,y⟩=⟨7\sec  t,\,7\tan  t⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{2} & =(7\sec  t)^{2}-(7\tan  t)^{2} \\  & =49(\sec^{2} t-\tan^{2} t) \\  & =49.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨7\sec  t,\,7\tan  t,\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $7\tan  t.$

The vector-valued function $f(t,z)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $2{y}^{2}-64{x}^{2}=128$ for $y\ge 8.$ What is the first component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the hyperbola

$$
2{y}^{2}-64{x}^{2}=128\,⇒\,\frac{{y}^{2}}{{8}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}}=1
$$

$$
⟨x,\,y⟩=⟨\sqrt{2}\tan  t,\,8\sec  t⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{{8}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}} & =\frac{(8\sec  t)^{2}}{64}-\frac{(\sqrt{2}\tan  t)^{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{64\sec^{2} t}{64}-\frac{2\tan^{2} t}{2} \\  & =\sec^{2} t-\tan^{2} t \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t,z) & =⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2}\tan  t,\,8\sec  t,\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $\sqrt{2}\tan  t.$
